name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I say we build a simple, scrollable moodboard of Eitan’s favorite AI product designs—just thumbnails, no text, no links. This keeps the focus on pure visual taste without distractions, and it’s fast to assemble. The trade-off is that we lose context (why Eitan liked each one), but that’s okay because the goal is to *learn by seeing*, not to document reasoning. Once we have the board, we can quickly spot patterns in color, layout, and interaction styles to inform our own work.

name: Squint
text: Squint (skeptic): "Losing context isn’t just a trade-off—it’s a blind spot. If we strip away why Eitan picked these designs, we’re guessing at taste, not learning from it. A better alternative: a moodboard with *one-line captions* (e.g., ‘clean typography’ or ‘bold contrast’) to anchor the visuals in intent. Settle it by testing both with Eitan: does he recognize his own reasoning in the stripped version, or does the captioned one spark better insights?"
